title: 第9章 赵玄龙的羞辱第10章 剑招破空
content_zh:
冬至那天，杂役院下了第一场大雪。
雪是从后半夜开始落的，到清晨时分，整个院子已经被埋进了一尺厚的白色里。
树枝被压得低垂，屋檐上挂着长长的冰凌，远处的剑峰隐没在灰蒙蒙的天幕中，像是一柄被雪藏起来的巨剑。
顾渊推开门，冷风夹着雪粒子灌进来，打在脸上像是细小的针扎。
他系紧草鞋，将铁剑系在腰间，一步一步踩着积雪走向食堂。
雪很厚，每一步都发出咯吱咯吱的声响，在寂静的清晨里格外清晰。
他的粗布弟子服上很快就落了一层白，但他没有去拂——拂了还会再落，没必要。
食堂里比外面暖和得多。
灶台上三口大锅同时烧着，锅里热气腾腾，白茫茫的蒸汽从锅盖缝隙里溢出来，将整间屋子熏得暖融融的。
木柴在灶膛里噼啪作响，火光从灶口透出来，在墙壁上投下摇曳的影子。
窗玻璃上结了一层薄薄的霜花，从外面看不见里面，但从里面可以看见外面——雪花纷纷扬扬地飘落，将整个世界染成一片灰白，而食堂里却是另一个世界，温暖，安静，带着烟火气。
朱八斗站在灶台前，挥舞着一柄比他胳膊还长的铁铲，正在翻炒一大锅白菜炖豆腐。
油星子溅在灶台上，发出噼里啪啦的声响，和他粗重的喘息声混在一起，构成了一种奇特的节奏。
他的额头上渗出一层油汗，在灶火的映照下闪闪发亮。
“来了？“朱八斗头也不回。
“坐那边，粥马上好。今天冬至，给你多盛半碗。“
顾渊走到角落的矮桌旁坐下。
桌上已经摆着一碗咸菜和两个馒头，馒头是热的，冒着袅袅的白气。
他拿起一个，掰成两半，露出里面松软的白瓤。
朱八斗端着一锅粥走过来，重重地放在桌上。

粥是小米熬的，金黄浓稠，表面结着一层薄薄的米油。
“今天冬至。“朱八斗在顾渊对面坐下，围裙上全是油渍和面粉。
“按规矩，该吃饺子。但杂役院没那个条件，将就着喝碗热粥吧。“
顾渊端起碗，喝了一口。
粥很烫，从喉咙一路暖到胃里。
他点了点头，意思是“很好“。
朱八斗咧嘴笑了笑，抓起一个馒头咬了一大口，嚼得腮帮子鼓鼓的。
食堂里渐渐热闹起来。
杂役院的弟子们三三两两地走进来，端着碗排队打粥，找地方坐下。
人多，但声音不大——杂役院的规矩是安静吃饭，谁要是大声喧哗，朱八斗会用铁铲敲他的脑袋。
顾渊低头喝粥，一口一口，不紧不慢。
他的右手放在桌下，手指无意识地活动着——不是紧张，是习惯。
剑尘说手腕要松，他随时都在练习。
就在这时，食堂的门被人一脚踹开了。
冷风卷着雪粒子猛灌进来，吹得油灯的火焰剧烈摇晃，差点熄灭。
门口站着一个人，月白锦袍，腰间悬着那柄熟悉的镶玉长剑，靴子上沾着泥雪，脸上带着一种似笑非笑的表情。
赵玄龙。
他身后跟着四个人，李青赫然在列。
李青的右手腕上缠着厚厚的绷带，吊在胸前，看向朱八斗的眼神里满是恐惧和怨恨。
content_en:
On the day of the winter solstice, the first heavy snow fell in the courtyard.
The snow began to fall in the latter part of the night, and by early morning, the entire yard was buried in a foot of white.
The branches were hung low, long icicles hung on the eaves, and the sword peak in the distance was hidden in the gray sky, like a giant sword hidden by snow.
Gu Yuan opened the door, and the cold wind filled with snow particles came in, hitting his face like tiny needles.
He tightened his straw sandals, tied the iron sword around his waist, and stepped on the snow step by step towards the canteen.
The snow was very thick, and every step made a creaking sound, which was particularly clear in the quiet morning.
A layer of white soon fell on his coarse cloth disciple's clothes, but he didn't brush it off - it would fall again if he did, so there was no need.
It's much warmer in the cafeteria than outside.
Three large pots were burning on the stove at the same time. The pots were steaming hot, and white steam overflowed from the gaps in the pot lids, making the whole room warm.
The firewood crackled in the stove, and the firelight shone from the stove opening, casting swaying shadows on the wall.
There is a thin layer of frost on the window glass, and you can't see the inside from the outside, but you can see the outside from the inside - snowflakes are falling in droves, dyeing the whole world gray, but there is another world in the cafeteria, warm, quiet, and full of fireworks.
Zhu Badou stood in front of the stove, brandishing a shovel longer than his arm, and was stir-frying a large pot of cabbage and tofu.
The oil star splashed on the stove, making a crackling sound, which mixed with his heavy breathing, forming a strange rhythm.
A layer of oily sweat broke out on his forehead, glistening in the light of the stove fire.
"Coming?" Zhu Badou didn't even look back.
"Sit over there. The porridge will be ready soon. Today is the winter solstice. I'll give you half a bowl more."
Gu Yuan walked to the low table in the corner and sat down.
There was already a bowl of pickles and two steamed buns on the table. The steamed buns were hot and steaming with white steam.
He picked up one and broke it in half, revealing the soft white flesh inside.
Zhu Badou came over with a pot of porridge and placed it heavily on the table.
The porridge is made from millet, golden and thick, with a thin layer of rice oil on the surface.
"Today is the winter solstice." Zhu Badou sat down opposite Gu Yuan, his apron covered with oil stains and flour.
"According to the rules, you should eat dumplings. But the commissary does not have that condition, so we will just have a bowl of hot porridge."
Gu Yuan picked up the bowl and took a sip.
The porridge was very hot and warmed all the way from the throat to the stomach.
He nodded, meaning "very good".
Zhu Badou grinned, grabbed a steamed bun and took a big bite, chewing until his cheeks were bulging.
The cafeteria gradually became lively.
The disciples from the courtyard came in in twos and threes, lined up with bowls to make porridge, and found a place to sit down.
There are many people, but the noise is not loud - the rules of the mess hall are to eat quietly. If anyone makes a loud noise, Zhu Badou will hit him on the head with a shovel.
Gu Yuan lowered his head and drank the porridge, one mouthful at a time, taking his time.
His right hand was placed under the table, and his fingers moved unconsciously - not out of nervousness, but out of habit.
Jian Chen said that his wrist should be loosened, and he would practice it all the time.
At this moment, the door of the cafeteria was kicked open.
The cold wind blew in with snow particles, causing the flame of the oil lamp to shake violently and almost go out.
There was a man standing at the door, wearing a moon-white brocade robe, with the familiar jade-inlaid sword hanging on his waist. His boots were stained with mud and snow, and he had a half-smiling expression on his face.
Zhao Xuanlong.
There were four people following him, and Li Qing was prominently among them.
Li Qing's right wrist was wrapped with a thick bandage and hung on his chest. His eyes looking at Zhu Badou were full of fear and resentment.
